gallery.filename: Former Railway Line, Tide Mills - geograph.org.uk - 592511.jpg
gallery.title: File:Former Railway Line, Tide Mills - geograph.org.uk - 592511.jpg
gallery.description: Former Railway Line, Tide Mills Laid in the 1880s to transport shingle from the beach to the help with the construction of the western breakwater just out of picture near the cliffs to the left. After that it was briefly used to collect blue boulders used in pottery glazes. The embedded line is now a footpath that runs from Newhaven to Seaford. The ruins are those of the former Chailey Marine Hospital, the hospital building on the left and the nurses home to the right.
categories: Disused railway lines in East Sussex

gallery.title: File:Mill Pond - geograph.org.uk - 592477.jpg
gallery.description: Mill Pond Once covered a much larger area and now just a shadow of its former self. Connected to Mill Creek through the small sluice gate. The remains in the foreground are the foundations from the former Chailey Marine Hospital nurses' home.

gallery.filename: Remains of Chailey Marine Hospital - geograph.org.uk - 592496.jpg
gallery.title: File:Remains of Chailey Marine Hospital - geograph.org.uk - 592496.jpg
gallery.description: Remains of Chailey Marine Hospital Built in 1924 as an extension of Chailey Heritage Hospital founded originally to provide for disabled and other handicapped children. The idea was to build a small hospital on the seafront as it was believed sea air was healthy. The foundations to the right were for the actual hospital whilst those further on the left were for the nurses home. Whilst the foundations were concrete the buildings were wooden. The hospital was evacuated and demolished with the rest of Tide Mills in 1940. The embankment on the extreme left was built to hold the waters of the mill pond in whilst Seaford lies straight ahead.

gallery.description: Ruins, Tide Mills Remnants of the wall of the former coal yard. The small slits visible in this wall and ithers were made by the Canadian Army when they used the area as atraining ground during World War Two.

gallery.title: File:Site of Former Mill, Tide Mills - geograph.org.uk - 592519.jpg
gallery.description: Site of Former Mill, Tide Mills Built in 1764 the mill reached its zenith during the 1830s and 40s. It closed in 1883 and was briefly used as a warehouse until 1900 before being demolished.

gallery.filename: Tide Mills Village - geograph.org.uk - 592375.jpg
gallery.title: File:Tide Mills Village - geograph.org.uk - 592375.jpg
gallery.description: Tide Mills Village Following Mill Drove into the ruined village. The first set of ruins to the right was the former Station Keeper's Cottage whilst those to the left were warehouses and yards. In the background is Castle Hill guarding the entrance to the Ouse.

gallery.filename: Tide Mills Village - geograph.org.uk - 592541.jpg
gallery.title: File:Tide Mills Village - geograph.org.uk - 592541.jpg
gallery.description:
Tide Mills Village Viewed from the site of the former mill. Whilst the mill may have been demolished in 1900 the village that grew up around it continued to operate. The ruins beyond the creek were turned into horse stables during the 1920s in order to rehabilitate race horses by getting them to run in the sea at low tides. A number of the cottages continued to be inhabitated until 1934 when the lack of sanitation and other utilities enabled the local council to condemn them. The last inhabitants were forcibly evicted in 1940 and the buildings destroyed so that the British Army could have a clear field of fire should the Wehrmacht choose Seaford Bay as a landing point.
Beyond the ruins to the left the concrete boards of the former Bishopstone Beach station can be made out whilst in the background is the modern suburb of Bishopstone built on Rookery Hill.

gallery.filename: Southern End of Mill Drove - geograph.org.uk - 718354.jpg
gallery.title: File:Southern End of Mill Drove - geograph.org.uk - 718354.jpg
gallery.description: Southern End of Mill Drove Now blocked to traffic at the level crossing this is now the far end of Tidemills village street though originally it would have continued eastwards towards the Chailey Marine Hospital. The rails once served a small line that collected shingle and was linked to the mainline near Newhaven Marine Station whilst the pond in the background is the remnants of the former millpond that powered the tide mill.
